stories.title: Falcons QB Michael Penix on track to start vs. Bears if no setbacks, coach says
stories.summary: Falcons quarterback Michael Penix Jr. will start Sunday against the Bears despite a rib injury, as long as there are no setbacks during the week.
stories.detail: FLOWERY BRANCH, Ga. -- Atlanta Falcons quarterback Michael Penix Jr . will start Sunday against the visiting Chicago Bears despite a rib injury, as long as there are no setbacks during the week, coach Kevin Stefanski said Wednesday. Penix said he made every throw in practice Wednesday and took all the first-team reps. He was listed by the Falcons as a full participant in practice. In Sunday night's home loss to the Baltimore Ravens , Penix took a big hit late in the fourth quarter and came out of the game. He returned one play later, but when the tie game went into overtime, Tua Tagovailoa entered as the Falcons' quarterback. The Ravens scored a touchdown on their first drive in OT, and Tagovailoa threw a game-ending interception. Penix had imaging done earlier this week, but Stefanski said he didn't want to get into specifics about the extent of the rib injury. Stefanski said Penix is "feeling better." Penix also didn't want to get into the specifics of the imaging done, just that it was positive news. "They're good," he said of his ribs. "They get better every day. I felt good today at practice and I know I'm going to continue to feel good. I just got to stay on top of my rehab …

stories.title: Patriots CB Gonzalez says he's 'ready to go'; WR Brown returns to practice
stories.summary: Patriots cornerback Christian Gonzalez said Wednesday he's ready to return after missing the past two games with a shoulder injury.
stories.detail: FOXBOROUGH, Mass. -- New England Patriots Pro Bowl cornerback Christian Gonzalez , who has missed the past two games due to a shoulder injury, said he will return for Sunday's home game against the New York Jets . "I'm good now, ready for Sunday," Gonzalez told reporters Wednesday. Gonzalez injured his shoulder in the team's Week 3 loss to the Jacksonville Jaguars and initially thought he was OK after the game. He explained Wednesday what unfolded in the days following the game. "At that point, you got a lot of adrenaline. Adrenaline covers a lot of things in this sport," he said. "At that time, I felt good. Things happen, so it is what it is and I'm ready for this week. "... I've been itching, kind of going a little crazy when I'm not getting to play. It's hard. You put in work with all these guys and then you don't get to be out there with them." Gonzalez watched the Patriots' 45-17 win over the Las Vegas Raiders this past Sunday from the sideline, saying it was important to him to be there for his teammates. teamStories.detail: The Raiders designated tight end Carter Runyon to return Wednesday, the team announced. It opens Runyon's 21-day practice window, and the team can activate him back to the active roster at any point in the next three weeks. Runyon went on injured reserve on Aug. 30 with an undisclosed injury after not playing in the preseason. He became eligible to return last week after missing four games. Runyon played 13 games last season, seeing action on 45 offensive snaps and 206 on special teams. He made two tackles and caught one pass for 3 yards.

stories.detail: The Kristaps Porziņģis mystery continued on Wednesday when the Golden State Warriors announced that the 31-year-old Latvian frontcourt standout will remain out indefinitely due to a “health-related matter” but will be around the team. It's still unclear what exactly Porziņģis is dealing with, a week away from Golden State's regular-season opener in Los Angeles against the Lakers. Porziņģis, the 2015 No. 4 overall pick whom the Warriors acquired in a trade with the Atlanta Hawks last season , put out a statement on social media not long after the organization released its latest update on the big man . “Hello people, I'm working with doctors and experts to figure out how to be fully back to good health asap,” the one-time All-Star and NBA champion wrote . “Honestly, I'm getting better and better. I just have to stay patient, and I believe I'll be feeling great again soon. ”It has definitely been frustrating dealing with some health stuff that you can't exactly pinpoint, on top of injuries throughout my career, so it has added up for sure, but we will get through it. ”Health is wealth.
